info.title: Arker Public VM API
info.description: Public VM and control-plane API contract. Every supported deployment exposes the same wire shapes. Features that are unavailable in a selected region or provider return an `ErrorResponse` with `code: "unsupported_operation"`.

tags.name: Policies
tags.description: Control inbound and outbound VM network access.

tags.name: Runs
tags.description: Execute commands and inspect their results.

tags.name: Sync
tags.description: Read and write files in a VM.

tags.name: Filesystems
tags.description: Create shared filesystems and mount them into VMs.

200.description: Service is ready to accept public API traffic.

503.description: Service is live but not currently ready to accept public API traffic.

get.description: Public health/readiness probe. The response body is intentionally minimal and does not expose host, region, release, or golden-image internals.

post.description: Create a new VM by forking from an existing VM ID or a VM name within an organization. Exactly one of `source_vm_id` or `source_vm_name` must be set. Forking a VM owned by another organization requires that VM to be public.

get.description: List VMs visible to the authenticated caller, optionally filtered by region, provider, owner, visibility, or lifecycle state.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Narrow to a single backend region (e.g. `us-west-2`). When omitted, the response aggregates across every configured region.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Narrow results to a cloud provider.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: List public VMs owned by this org. Currently only `ArkerHQ` is supported, together with `public=true`, for the public template catalog.

parameters.name: public
parameters.description: Filter by public visibility. Use with `org_id=ArkerHQ` to list the public template catalog.

200.description: VMs visible to the authenticated caller.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unix epoch seconds; include runs at or after this time.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Unix epoch seconds; include runs before this time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of rows to return.

parameters.name: lite
parameters.description: When true, omit large input/output previews where supported by the backend.

200.description: Runs visible to the authenticated caller across VMs, providers, and regions.

get.description: Control-plane listing of run activity visible to the authenticated caller across VMs, providers, and regions.
Return one VM visible to the authenticated caller.

delete.description: Delete a VM owned by the authenticated caller.

patch.description: Update a VM's resources, SSH keys, or network policy.

get.description: Return the VM's network policy together with its derived inbound exposure and enforcement metadata.

200.description: The VM's policy document (empty when none is set), plus its derived inbound exposure (reachability + per-port tunnels).

put.description: Replace the VM's complete network policy and apply it to the running VM.

200.description: Stored policy, plus the domains it escalates to MITM and any degrade warnings.

post.description: Run a command. Foreground execution is the portable baseline. Set `background` to return a pollable run immediately. A request with `signal` targets the selected persistent session's foreground process group, does not execute `command`, and returns an acknowledgement without a run id. Optional session, signal, resource-lifecycle, policy, and per-run resource controls may return `unsupported_operation` on backends that do not support them.

get.description: List recorded runs for one VM, with optional lifecycle and time filters.
Return one recorded run, including its current state and available output.

delete.description: Request cancellation of an in-flight run.

get.description: List persistent command sessions for one VM.

post.description: Create a persistent command session in a VM.

patch.summary: Update a session (resize PTY / set timeout)
patch.description: Resize the session's PTY (cols/rows) and/or update its idle timeout. Resize is delivered to a LIVE attached PTY in-band; if the PTY is detached, it is applied directly to the session's runtime; if no PTY has ever attached, the call is accepted as a no-op. REST equivalent of the WebSocket {"type":"resize"} control frame — usable from any client, attached or not.

delete.description: Close and remove a persistent VM session.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Single executable path to launch (no shell-splitting). Defaults to the login shell.

parameters.name: persist
parameters.description: When true (default), disconnecting keeps the shell running so the same session_id can reconnect to it and receive recent scrollback. When false, the shell is terminated on disconnect. A kill control message or the configured idle TTL terminates a persistent shell.

parameters.name: cancel_ttl_secs
parameters.description: Destroy the PTY after this many seconds without terminal input or output. Omit or set to zero to disable this PTY-specific idle limit.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Browser auth: a short-lived ticket from POST .../pty-ticket, used in place of the Authorization header (which a browser WebSocket cannot set).

get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket carrying an interactive pseudo-terminal in the VM, reusing the same in-guest PTY as SSH. Authenticate with a bearer API key or, for browser clients, a short-lived PTY ticket. Reopening the same `session_id` reconnects to a persistent shell and replays recent scrollback. Binary server frames contain raw terminal output; binary client frames contain stdin bytes. Text client frames accept JSON controls for `resize`, `kill`, and `ping`. Closing the socket detaches a persistent shell or destroys a non-persistent shell; `kill` always destroys it. The service enforces attachment limits and closes oversized or idle connections.

101.description: Switching Protocols — the WebSocket PTY stream is established.

post.description: Returns a short-lived, multi-use credential for opening the PTY WebSocket from a browser, which cannot set an Authorization header. The bearer-authenticated caller must own the VM. Pass the returned credential as the `ticket` query parameter on the PTY WebSocket URL.

Create a persistent sync: ensure a Filesystem exists (creating
one if requested) and bind-mount it into this VM at `path`.
Bidirectional by virtue of being a mount — there is no separate
sync-direction parameter. Returns `ErrorResponse` code
`conflict` if a sync already exists at `path`.

get.description: List persistent filesystem mounts for one VM, optionally filtered by filesystem.

delete.description: Remove a persistent filesystem mount from a VM.

200.description: Read or write result, matching the request op.

post.description:
Read or write files in the VM filesystem. Op-discriminated:
`{op:"read",path}` reads a file (inline content for small files, a
presigned GET URL for large ones); `{op:"write",writes:[...]}` writes,
each entry an inline chunk or a presigned-upload step. Binding a
filesystem into the VM is the separate `/v1/vms/{id}/syncs` resource.

get.description: List shared filesystems visible to the authenticated caller.

post.description: Create a shared filesystem owned by the authenticated caller's organization.

get.description: Return one shared filesystem visible to the authenticated caller.

delete.description: Delete a shared filesystem after all VM mounts have been removed.

200.description: Delete result. The filesystem must not be mounted by any VM (no remaining `Sync` referencing it).

PtyTicket.name: ticket
PtyTicket.description: Short-lived browser credential created by the PTY ticket endpoint.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes run submission safely retryable. Reusing a key with the same request returns the original result; reusing it with a different request returns a conflict.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by the previous page's `next_cursor`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Max items per page. Backend caps may apply.

RetryAfter.description: Delay in seconds before retrying a transiently unavailable request.

PaymentRequired.description: The organization must complete billing setup or payment before starting new compute.

UnsupportedOperation.description: The request is valid, but this backend does not support the requested operation or option.

error.message: background runs are not supported on this backend

status.description: Readiness status. `ok` means the service is ready; other values may be returned with HTTP 503.

timestamp.description: Server time when the health response was generated.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code. `unsupported_operation` means the backend doesn't implement the requested optional feature. `payment_required` means billing setup or payment is required before new compute can start.

message.description: Human-readable, client-safe error message. For `code: "internal"`, this is intentionally generic.

timestamp.description: Server time when the error response was generated.

retry_after.description: Suggested retry delay in seconds. Present on retryable responses and mirrored by the Retry-After header.

operation.description: Operation that failed, when the backend can identify it safely.

runtime.description: Runtime involved in the failure, when safe to expose.

provider.description: Infrastructure provider involved in the failure, when safe to expose.

retryable.description: Whether clients should retry the operation.

VmState.description: Unified lifecycle state for a VM or a Session. `idle` means no command is currently executing; `running` means a command is in flight.

RunState.description:
Lifecycle state for a Run. `running` = command in flight.
`completed` = the command ran to completion; `exit_code` conveys
success (0) or a non-zero program exit (a non-zero exit is still
`completed`). `failed` = the platform could not run or finish the
command (host died, evicted mid-run, exec error); `fail_reason`
explains why, distinct from the program's `stderr`. `cancelled` =
cancelled by the client.

PolicyDoc.description: A VM's network policy document: an ordered, first-match-wins rule list for outbound and inbound traffic. An empty `policies` list uses the default posture: allow outbound traffic and require Arker authentication for inbound traffic. When a non-empty policy has no matching rule for a direction, traffic in that direction is denied. Use an explicit catch-all allow rule to express default-allow behavior.

secrets.description: Named secrets referenced by `${secret:NAME}` in a `rewrite` action's host/path/header/body values. Encrypted at rest with the rest of the document and REDACTED (masked with `***`) whenever the doc is echoed back on GET — so a GET response is NOT round-trippable back into a PUT without re-supplying real secret values.

hostname.description: Read-only (response-only). The single per-VM base hostname on the .app customer plane (<vm>.<region>.arker.app), present when the data-plane domain is configured — its presence is what signals the VM is reachable inbound. Reach a guest desktop at https://<hostname>:6080/. (The control plane — the API and SSH — stays on .ai.) Ignored on write.

mitm_domains.description: Read-only (response-only). Domains the policy escalates to the MITM proxy. Ignored on write.

warnings.description: Read-only (response-only). Non-fatal notes (e.g. rules degraded where the MITM data path is not active). Ignored on write.

PolicyEntry.description: One policy rule. `match` AND's its present fields (absent ⇒ catch-all).

type.description: Traffic direction: `outbound` controls connections initiated by the VM; `inbound` exposes a guest port. Unknown values are rejected.

auth.description: Authentication for an inbound allow rule. `open` exposes the port publicly; `arker` requires an API key for the caller's organization before forwarding to the guest. The default is `arker`. This field is invalid on deny and outbound rules. Inbound port matches must use individual ports rather than ranges.

PolicyMatch.description: Match criteria: present fields AND'd; list items OR'd. `ips` and `hosts` are mutually exclusive. L4 fields = ports/ips/hosts; L7 fields = methods/paths/headers/body_contains. A rule with any L7 field is enforced at the request layer by the managed MITM proxy; where the proxy is not active for a VM the rule degrades to its host/L4 projection — allow → host-allow, deny/rewrite → fail-closed deny.

ports.description: Single ports and/or inclusive [start, end] ranges, e.g. [80, 443, [1000, 2000]]. Empty/absent = any port.

hosts.description: Label-boundary suffix match on the request host: `github.com` matches `api.github.com`, not `evilgithub.com`.

headers.description: Header name → any-of values (names AND'd, a name's values OR'd).

oneOf.description: A mutating action: at least one of `rewrite` / `gate` must be present. The request is forwarded upstream (applying `rewrite` if present); a `gate` blocks it until an outbound HTTP check allows it.

PolicyAction.description: allow / deny, a mutating object `{ rewrite?, gate? }`, or `{ scaling: { suspend? } }`. Mutating and scaling actions need the MITM data-path.

ScalingAction.description: Auto-scaling behavior for matched outbound traffic. The object is extensible with future scaling controls.

suspend.description: Suspend the VM while a matched upstream request is blocked, then resume it when the response arrives.

Rewrite.description: Mutate-and-forward. Host/path/header/body values support request-time `$`-token interpolation: `$domain`, `$path`, `$method`, `$vm_id`, `$body` (the request body as received, also `${…}`-braced), and `$$` for a literal `$`. Unknown/unresolved tokens pass through unchanged.

body.description: Replace the request body entirely with this (interpolated) value; `$body` re-injects the original body. Absent = body forwarded unchanged.

Gate.description: `action.gate` performs an outbound HTTP authorization check before opening the VM's matching connection. A response status in `allow_on_status` permits the connection and applies any sibling `rewrite`; any other status denies it. Timeouts and connection failures follow `deny_on_timeout`, which defaults to deny. `path`, header values, and string leaves of `body` support `$` substitution with the documented request variables. `host` is not substituted. Injected JSON values are escaped, and gate requests reject private, link-local, and internal destinations.

host.description: Target endpoint INCLUDING scheme, e.g. https://authz.example.com. Not interpolated.

headers.description: Request headers (values interpolated). A stored credential (e.g. authorization) is encrypted at rest and REDACTED on policy read-back.

body.description: JSON request body; string leaves are interpolated and JSON-escaped. Absent = no body.

allow_on_status.description: HTTP status codes that mean ALLOW. Any other status denies. Must be non-empty.

deny_on_timeout.description: Verdict on timeout / connection failure: true = deny (fail-closed, default), false = allow (fail-open).

timeout_ms.description: Max wall-clock for the gate call before it is abandoned (then deny_on_timeout applies). Default ~30000.

source_vm_id.description: Global VM identifier. Org is inferred from the row.

source_vm_name.description: VM name within an org. Defaults `source_org_id` to the caller's org. A different org must be either the Arker org (for public goldens such as `ubuntu`) or one with a `public: true` VM by that name.

source_org_id.description: Optional explicit org context for `source_vm_name`. SDK auto-fills the Arker org when forking the public goldens.

name.description: Optional name for the new VM, scoped to the caller's org.

public.description: Make the new VM publicly forkable from other orgs.

ssh_public_keys.description: SSH public keys to authorize on the new VM as raw `authorized_keys` entries, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@host`. The list becomes the VM's authorized-key set. Omit it or pass an empty list to create the VM with no keys; add keys later with `PATCH /v1/vms/{id}`. Configure inbound reachability through the VM's policy.

platforms.description: Desired platform(s) when forking a golden, e.g. ["graviton3"] or a flexible set ["graviton2","graviton3"]. The fork is scheduled onto a host serving one of these, intersected with the platforms the golden is baked for. Optional: omit (null) or pass an empty list for no preference — the router picks from the golden's available platforms, weighted by host availability. Requesting a platform the golden isn't baked for returns 400. Ignored when forking an existing VM, which inherits its parent's platform.

policies.description: Network policy for the new VM. Omit it to inherit the source VM's policy. Providing a policy replaces the inherited policy; an empty document selects the default posture of allow-all outbound traffic and authenticated inbound traffic. Network topology is inherited from the source. Set SSH keys through `ssh_public_keys`.

resources.description: Resource shape for the new VM.

env.description: Optional environment-variable overrides for this session.

public.description: When `true`, other orgs can fork this VM (but cannot run on it).

root_source_vm_id.description: ID of the root (deepest-ancestor) source VM, if this VM was created by a chain of forks. None for VMs forked directly from an image.

root_source_vm_name.description: Name of the root source VM. Populated together with `root_source_vm_id`.

network.description: The VM's network object — SSH keys only. Inbound reachability and per-port tunnels are derived from `policies` and surface on the policies GET/PUT response, not here.

max_vcpus.description: Hard vCPU ceiling for a fork of this VM (KVM slot count). Requesting more fails the run.

min_vcpus.description: Smallest vCPU count accepted for this VM.

max_memory_mib.description: Hard memory ceiling (MiB) a fork can hotplug up to.

min_disk_mib.description: Smallest disk size (MiB) accepted for this VM. `0` means nodisk.

max_disk_mib.description: Largest disk size (MiB) accepted for this VM. `0` means nodisk.

cols.description: New terminal width in columns. Provide together with rows.

rows.description: New terminal height in rows. Provide together with cols.

timeout_secs.description: Idle auto-cancel window for the PTY; applies on the next attach.

timeout.description: Execution/kill bound in seconds: max wall-clock time the command runs before the host kills it. Omitted defaults to 3600 (1 hour). 0 explicitly disables the bound. Separate from the HTTP sync window — see time_to_background.

time_to_background.description: Sync window in seconds: how long the HTTP call blocks before backgrounding the run and returning a pollable run_id. Omitted defaults to 30. Does not bound command runtime — that is timeout.

acquire.description:
Comma-separated list of resources to ensure are
pre-allocated (warm) before the run starts. Values: `cpu`,
`memory`, `disk`. Example: `"cpu,memory"`.

release.description:
Comma-separated list of resources to release after the run
finishes. Values: `cpu`, `memory`, `disk`. `"cpu"` frees
vCPU but keeps memory hot for the next run on this VM;
`"cpu,memory,disk"` is a full release (closest to a
suspend).

signal.description: Deliver a signal to the selected persistent session's foreground process group. When set, the service does not execute `command`; it returns a completed acknowledgement with no run id. Use `session_id` or `session_idx` to select the session.

policies.description: Network policy applied to the VM before this run and retained afterward. A non-empty document replaces the persisted policy; an empty document selects the default posture of allow-all outbound traffic and authenticated inbound traffic. Omit it to use the current policy unchanged. If the policy cannot be stored and applied, the command does not run.

run_id.description: The run's own id. Present for executed runs; absent for operation acks (release/signal) with no run record.

state.description: Lifecycle state — "completed" for this shape. Read this (not the variant) for completion, uniformly with the run-status (`Run`) shape.

stdout_encoding.description: Encoding used for stdout. Valid UTF-8 is returned directly; arbitrary bytes are base64 encoded.

stderr_encoding.description: Encoding used for stderr. Valid UTF-8 is returned directly; arbitrary bytes are base64 encoded.

memory_requested_mib.description: Requested total memory in MiB when this run included a memory override. Absent when no override was requested.

memory_achieved_mib.description: Achieved total memory in MiB after applying the run's memory override. A memory reduction is best-effort, so this value can exceed `memory_requested_mib` when guest pages cannot be released. Absent when no override was requested.

memory_partial.description: True when a requested memory reduction was only partially applied. The command runs with the achieved allocation, and `memory_achieved_mib` reports that allocation. Defaults to false.

state.description: Lifecycle state — "running" for a backgrounded run.

fail_reason.description: System failure explanation when `state` is `failed` (e.g. "host died: <id>", "evicted mid-run"). Distinct from `stderr`, which is the program's own error output. Null for runs that ran to completion.

stdout_encoding.description: Encoding used for stdout. Valid UTF-8 is returned directly; arbitrary bytes are base64 encoded.

stderr_encoding.description: Encoding used for stderr. Valid UTF-8 is returned directly; arbitrary bytes are base64 encoded.

fail_reason.description: System failure explanation when `state` is `failed` — see `Run.fail_reason`. Distinct from the program's `stderr`.

pty.description: Mark this session for an interactive PTY. The PTY stream is attached separately through the session WebSocket endpoint.

cols.description: Advisory initial terminal width in columns. The WebSocket attach query may override it.

rows.description: Advisory initial terminal height in rows. The WebSocket attach query may override it.

command.description: Advisory command for an interactive PTY session.

path.description: VM-side path where the filesystem is mounted.

gpu_sms.description: GPU slice size: number of streaming multiprocessors (SMs) the VM may use. Only valid when the VM targets a GPU platform (e.g. "x86_64-a40"). Requesting more SMs than the physical GPU has returns 400. Omit for the host's default slice size.

gpu_vram_mib.description: GPU slice size: VRAM cap in MiB. Only valid when the VM targets a GPU platform. Requesting more VRAM than the physical GPU has returns 400. Omit for the host's default slice size.

NetworkInput.description: SSH key configuration for a fork or patch. Inbound reachability is controlled by the VM's policy document and reported by the policy endpoints.

ssh_public_keys.description: OpenSSH public keys authorized for terminator auth and in-VM sshd injection.

VmNetwork.description: A VM's network object: SSH keys ONLY. Inbound reachability, the .app hostname, and per-port tunnels are DERIVED from the VM's policy doc and surface on the policies GET/PUT response (the PolicyDoc's read-only fields), not here.

ssh_public_keys.description: Authorized SSH keys with fingerprints. Returned by GET /v1/vms/{id}; omitted from list responses when empty.

policies.description: Network policy for the VM. A non-empty document replaces the persisted policy and applies it to the running VM. An empty document selects the default posture of allow-all outbound traffic and authenticated inbound traffic. Omit it to leave the current policy unchanged. If the policy cannot be stored and applied, the request fails.
